prior_runtime_attempt.observed: G5 92/93 passed; the failing recovery call returned stale after the test reused a 1-second lease for the new recovery claim. The retained filesystem evidence shows orphan staging plus a complete final marker and four children.
prior_runtime_attempt.technical_basis: WorkspaceService.finish returns stale when its generation/token/state/unexpired compare-and-set affects no row. The test had a killed owner with a 1-second lease and gave the replacement claim the same 1-second lease; slow marker publication/layout can exhaust the replacement lease. The recorded gate did not capture exact claim-expiry timing, so this remains an evidence-based diagnosis rather than a directly observed expiry timestamp.
prior_runtime_attempt.repair: The approved fixture-only recovery-lease change is recorded in the preserved failed-gate follow-up; the historical gate remains failed and this ledger makes no pass claim from it.
prior_runtime_attempt.remaining_risk: A 10-second recovery lease may still be insufficient on extremely slow storage or severe host stalls; the fixture must fail rather than weaken the stale fence if completion exceeds the lease. Dedicated live/stale lease tests remain unchanged.

g5_phase_diagnostic_revision.observed: G5 hit its 300-second phase cap after 71 progress dots and before JUnit emission; the retained PostgreSQL temporary root shows test_sigkill_worker_crash_reco0 through reco10 completed their worker setup, while reco11 had only migration/profile fixtures and no crash-worker config or workspace root. Test source order places reco11 at workspace_before_claim, before the child worker launch. The exact in-test blocking call is not logged. The v2 timing comparison supplied for review reports crash configs began at +212.05 seconds versus v1 +143.89 seconds before the recovery branch, with subsequent 5–12-second gaps through +293.78 seconds.
g5_phase_diagnostic_revision.technical_basis: Seventy-one completed cases plus a newly created next-case fixture at the cumulative 300-second cutoff indicates phase-budget exhaustion, not an evidenced single-case overrun. The preserved records do not establish host pressure or prove the exact blocking operation. Keep the existing H2 25-second body plus 5-second cleanup watchdog; do not add a hard per-case interrupt for the historical 351 cases. They are rejected if their total duration exceeds 30 seconds after completion, while hung cases remain bounded by the unchanged 300-second phase caps. Progress events expose the active case when a phase is interrupted.
g5_phase_diagnostic_revision.repair: This historical revision led to the current six-phase progress accounting and G5 600-second cumulative budget. The current phase names, 407 IDs, caps and watchdog constraints are defined only by this ledger’s method and phases.
g5_phase_diagnostic_revision.remaining_risk: The 600-second G5 phase cap is an evidence-based allowance for measured cumulative suite latency, not evidence that host performance is stable. No host-pressure cause is proven. A historical case that exceeds 30 seconds is identified as over-bound only on completion; a hung case is interrupted by the phase cap and its current node is identified by the journal.
